item.title: Kinrin Lake, Yufuin — Guide
item.description: Kinrin Lake (Kinrin-ko) is the scenic centrepiece at the end of Yufuin’s main street and one of the town’s most beloved sights. Fed by both hot-spring and cold-water sources, the small lake stays relatively warm, and on cool mornings — especially in autumn and winter — a beautiful mist rises off its surface, giving the lake an ethereal, dreamlike quality that draws photographers at dawn. Its name, meaning ‘golden scales lake’, comes from the way the setting sun once made the fish scales glint like gold.

item.title: Nagasaki Night View from Mount Inasa — Guide
item.description: Nagasaki’s night view is celebrated as one of the ‘top three night views of Japan’, and the finest place to see it is the observation deck atop Mount Inasa (Inasayama), which rises 333 metres directly behind the city. Because Nagasaki is built around a harbour and up steep surrounding slopes, the lights of homes, streets and ships spill down the hillsides and ring the dark water like a giant jewel box or, as locals say, a ‘ten-million-dollar’ panorama.

item.title: Shikisai-no-oka Flower Hills — Guide
item.description: Shikisai-no-oka (‘Hills of Seasonal Colour’) is a spectacular flower garden set on the rolling hills of Biei in central Hokkaido, famous for its vast, undulating patchwork of vividly coloured flower fields. Across some 15 hectares, broad stripes of blooms — lavender, poppies, salvia, marigolds, sunflowers, lupins and many more — carpet the hillsides in bands of colour that shift through the summer and autumn, set against a backdrop of the Tokachi mountain range and Biei’s iconic gently rolling farmland.

item.title: The Bungo Strait Coast — Guide
item.description: The Bungo Strait (Bungo Suido) is the stretch of sea separating eastern Kyushu from the island of Shikoku, and Oita’s long coastline along it offers scenic beauty and superb seafood. The strait’s strong tidal currents, where the waters of the Seto Inland Sea meet the Pacific, create rich, oxygenated fishing grounds that produce some of Japan’s most prized fish — above all the famous ‘Seki-saba’ (mackerel) and ‘Seki-aji’ (horse mackerel) caught off Saganoseki, so firm and flavourful they command premium prices nationwide.

item.title: The Seto Inland Sea Island Landscape — Guide
item.description: The Seto Inland Sea (Setouchi) is one of Japan’s most beloved landscapes, a vast, calm, sheltered sea enclosed by Honshu, Shikoku and Kyushu and studded with hundreds of green islands large and small. Long a highway of trade and culture, its serene beauty — gentle water, layered island silhouettes, fishing boats and famous sunsets — has inspired poets, artists and travellers for centuries. Kagawa sits right on its shore, and the seascape shapes everything: the ferries fanning out to the islands, the great bridges (like the Seto Ohashi) leaping across it, the island communities and the art destinations of Naoshima and beyond.
